pages.text: Today was sheep-shearing day. Mom clipped with scissors in the yard.
Shorn sheep looked skinny. "I will bring all the unshorn ones." Pipo climbed the hill.
Mrs. Goose stretched her neck. "I saw them all! That sheep has not been shorn."
The sheep she pointed to was skinny. It had already been shorn.
"Then that one over there!" That sheep was skinny too.
A skinny sheep lined up in the yard a second time. Mom smiled, holding her scissors. "I sheared this one earlier!"
"I saw them all! Probably... I think?" Mrs. Goose's neck drew back little by little.
Pipo looked around the hill, watching only the fluffy sheep.
He led the fluffy ones down to the yard. They lined up like soft clouds.
Even the last fluffy one became skinny. Shorn wool piled up like a mountain. Mrs. Goose plopped onto it. "Oh, so soft!"
